subject: Launchpad co-marketing stipend & credit-split question
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@launchpadhub.co>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Avi Patel <avi@seedfoundry.org>
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood participation — stipend vs credits question

Hi Irene —

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. Launchpad is finalizing our partner package for the upcoming cohort and we have two related asks where we could use clarification from Redwood before we lock the term sheet:

1) Program stipend: we typically offer a modest co-marketing stipend (~$7k) to cover event sponsorship and joint PR. Can Redwood treat that as a billable credit (applied to usage) instead of a cash payment?
2) Credit splitting: a few of our teams are multi-product and want to split the $10k trial credit between two sub-accounts (one for backend inference, one for embeddings). Is split/apply-to-subaccount supported, and will it affect eligibility for the Dedicated discounted tier?

Attached: Launchpad-Program-Terms-v3.pdf with the overall partner flow.

Appreciate any guidance — cohort kickoff is 9/4 so timelines are tight.

Best,
Maya Singh
Partnerships, Launchpad Hub

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya@launchpadhub.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood participation — stipend vs credits question

Hi Maya —

Great to hear from you. Short answers up front and then a few implementation notes:

- Stipend as credits: yes, we can convert a co-marketing stipend into platform credits for the cohort, but there are two caveats — (1) credits must be attached to a company account (not paid to individuals), and (2) credits applied to Dedicated commitments are treated differently for billing/recognition (accounting wants to track as contra-revenue). We can accommodate both but need to flag for finance.

- Splitting credits: we support allocating credits across sub-accounts but it requires the accounts to be on the same top-level billing entity and for the split to be recorded in our billing table prior to activation. It does not automatically change Dedicated eligibility, but if a team wants Dedicated pricing on a sub-account, that sub-account must meet the minimum commit independently.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben, can you confirm whether converting stipend->credits triggers any legal/contractual review from billing (we may need a short amendment)?
- Marissa, can you propose the UX flow for allocating credits to two sub-accounts (one-time split vs percentage over time)?

Maya — if you can share the final cohort company list (and which sub-accounts need splits) we can generate a draft credit allocation that finance can sign off on.

Thanks —
Irene
Head of Partnerships Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Maya Singh <maya@launchpadhub.co>
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 13:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood participation — stipend vs credits question

Irene / Maya —

Finance is okay with stipend->credits conversion but asks for a simple amendment clause: credits issued in lieu of cash are non-refundable, expire after 12 months, and cannot be transferred outside the parent billing entity. We also need the partner to confirm that the stipend is not tied to any tax/withholding obligations we would otherwise have for a cash payment.

On Dedicated eligibility: converting the stipend to credits doesn't provide an automatic pass to Dedicated pricing. The sub-account would need to meet the standard minimum sustained commit. If Launchpad wants to guarantee cohort participants can access Dedicated at a special committed rate, we can model a temporary promotional floor — but that requires a reserved-seat/commit schedule on our side. That is doable but needs an SOW.

I'll loop Legal if needed but I think the amendment text will be straightforward.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Exec, Startups
Redwood Inference

From: Maya Singh <maya@launchpadhub.co>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Avi Patel <avi@seedfoundry.org>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Aug 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood participation — stipend vs credits question

Thanks Ben / Irene — this is helpful. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The stipend is paid by Launchpad Hub; we'd prefer credits applied to the cohort lead account (Launchpad Labs LLC) and then allocated to startups. Launchpad will record distribution internally for tax purposes — fine for Redwood to treat them as non-refundable credits that expire in 12 months.
- For Dedicated: we don't want to force early stage startups into Reserved commits. Ideally Redwood would offer a temporary "cohort access" to Dedicated at a reduced commit floor (e.g., half our standard min) for the duration of the 3-month program. That would be a short promotional exception.

Attached is a draft co-marketing proposal (Redwood-CoMarketing-Proposal.xlsx) showing how we imagine credits distributed across 10 startups and the proposed 3-month Dedicated trial.

Can we get a pricing model/impact by EOD Fri so we can finalize program terms?

Best,
Maya

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya@launchpadhub.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Sep 2028 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood participation — stipend vs credits question

Maya —

Thanks for the proposal and the worksheet — this helped. Final notes and commitments from Redwood side:

1) Credits: we will issue a $7,000 co-marketing credit to the Launchpad lead account, and $10,000 in cohort credits to be distributed across startups according to your attached split. Credits will be non-refundable, valid for 12 months, and can be split across sub-accounts as long as they remain under the same top-level billing entity.

2) Dedicated trial exception: Redwood will provide a promotional Dedicated access tier for cohort startups with a temporary reduced minimum commit of 50% of our standard min for the 3-month program. This exception is limited to Launchpad cohort participants and expires at the end of the program. If a startup wants to continue on Dedicated after the trial, they must sign the normal commit terms.

3) Legal/billing: Ben will draft a one-page amendment capturing the stipend->credits conversion, expiration, and non-transferability. Once you sign, we will provision credits and enable the sub-account allocation UI.

4) Ops/activation: Marissa — please prepare the allocation flow: we need (a) a CSV upload for the cohort list, (b) allocation percentages per sub-account, and (c) a PO/DocuSign flow for the amendment. Maya, we'll send a DocuSign link and a HubSpot deal record this week (see related_links).

If that sounds right I can get Legal to review and send the DocuSign. We aim to have credits live by 9/25 to match your cohort onboarding.

Appreciate the partnership — excited to run this.

Irene Choi
Head of Partnerships Ops
Redwood Inference
